clue.text: Uproar when spirit drink's knocked back

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

indicators.note: knocked back, as a drink is downed, says the word for drink is turned round

parts.note: to sup is to drink; the 's stands for 'is' and joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene breaks out once the rum is downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reads like downing a drink in one, which fits the surface, but here it turns the drink word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion, a direct synonym for an uproar.

clue.text: Union raise matter about manager behind take over

indicators.note: about says the reversed matter wraps round the letter from manager
in a down clue, raise means the word for matter is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: pus is the matter of an infected wound

indicators.note: behind means the rear of the word manager, its last letter

explanation.surface: A trade union stirs up trouble over a manager in a takeover dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' turns PUS into SUP, and 'about' puts R, the back of 'manager', inside it to make SURP.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize power or a position wrongfully, i.e. to take it over.

clue.text: Writer in Australia retired acquiring long strip of land out to sea

definitions.text: strip of land out to sea

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a crossword staple for writer

indicators.note: acquiring says the reversed country takes in the letter for long
retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters for Australia are reversed

explanation.surface: An author living in Australia retires to a long spit of land by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns AUS into SUA, which 'acquiring' fills with L to give SULA.
explanation.definitionFit: A peninsula is land almost surrounded by water, jutting out into the sea.

clue.text: Son informed about his heart is showing no emotion

indicators.note: about says the word for informed goes round the letter from his

parts.note: if someone is informed, they have been told

indicators.note: heart means the middle letter of the word his

explanation.surface: A son, told about his father's heart condition, stays impassive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' gives I, the centre of 'his', which 'about' places inside TOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid describes someone impassive and unexcitable, giving little outward sign of feeling.

clue.text: Quiet diplomacy protecting international vessel

indicators.note: protecting means the word for diplomacy surrounds and shields the letter for international

parts.note: tact is skill and sensitivity in dealing with people, like diplomacy
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Discreet diplomacy shields an international ship from scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' means the diplomacy word wraps round the single letter for international.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means habitually reserved and saying little, so a quiet person.

clue.text: Lounge seating for trio's musical sequence

parts.note: a trio is a set of three pieces; the 's means 'is', joining the parts
a suite is a sequence of musical movements

explanation.surface: A sofa set doubles as a chamber group's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a matching sofa and two armchairs, the standard set of seating for a living room.

clue.text: Game to tease boy in lock-up

indicators.note: in says the tease and boy letters go inside the lock-up

parts.note: a cage is somewhere to lock up an animal or prisoner
to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Mocking a lad who has been thrown in a cell is all a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the tease and boy letters inside the lock-up word, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: Part of fork's secured with gardening string

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so the prong holds the letter for with inside it

parts.note: a tine is one of the prongs of a fork

explanation.surface: A garden fork's prong is fastened with some garden string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured' puts W inside TINE, after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is strong thread used by gardeners to tie plants to stakes.

clue.text: Take extraordinary umbrage about unknown trainee starting in Wasps, say

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the unknown and the trainee's first letter
extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the letters of umbrage are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

indicators.note: starting means the first letter of trainee

explanation.surface: A trainee joining the Wasps squad is deeply offended by something unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges umbrage and 'about' wraps it round the unknown and the trainee's first letter. Wasps are an English rugby union club, not insects here.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps is the name of a professional English rugby union club, so an example of the side.

clue.text: Question a new function for non-governmental body

parts.note: to go is to function or work, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone questions the purpose of a new non-governmental agency.
explanation.walkthrough: A quango, a semi-independent public body, is a familiar British term.
explanation.definitionFit: A quango is a quasi-autonomous non-governmental organisation, funded by but independent of government.

clue.text: Fencing's poor following river south

indicators.note: following says the word for poor comes after the river letter

parts.note: someone in poor health is ailing

explanation.surface: A fence beside a river to the south is in poor repair.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Fencing's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Railings are a fence built of upright bars, so a form of fencing.

clue.text: Dentist's request to have extra work space going ahead

indicators.note: going ahead means the work and space letters are put in front of the extra

parts.note: OP is the abbreviation for opus, a work
an en is a printer's space, half an em
a wide is an extra in cricket, a run given for a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach

explanation.surface: A dentist asks for more room to work on the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is an extra run conceded for a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach; an en is a printer's space.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist asks a patient to part their jaws as far as possible, so the phrase is the typical request.

clue.text: The old bishop's found inside, near to the final farewell

indicators.note: found inside says the old the and the bishop go within the other pieces

parts.note: by means near to, as in standing by the door
ye is an archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; the 's means 'is'

indicators.note: final points to the last letter of the second the

explanation.surface: An old bishop says goodbye at the final service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found inside' puts the old-style article and the bishop together within the near-to piece, just after its first letter; 'final' takes the end of the second 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled word is an informal goodbye, so it can stand for a farewell.

clue.text: You once hid in boathouse

indicators.note: hid in says the letters are concealed inside the word boathouse

explanation.surface: Someone recalls how they once hid inside a boathouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hid' looks like part of the story but signals the concealed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the archaic singular form of you, used in older English.

clue.text: Call cab in wintry weather on stretch in Great North Road

parts.note: hail is icy precipitation of winter

indicators.note: in says the word for stretch goes inside the road's name

parts.note: the A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, historically called the Great North Road; A and the numeral 1 read as AI
to tax is to stretch or strain, as in taxing one's patience

explanation.surface: Someone flags a taxi as hail strikes along the Great North Road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's main London to Edinburgh road, the Great North Road; 1 reads as I, and TAX goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag down a taxi is to call one, the phrase meaning summon a cab.

clue.text: Took in food and papers collecting confused gent's key

indicators.note: collecting means the papers gather the other letters inside them

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: confused means the letters of gent's are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A muddled gentleman has eaten and taken his papers and a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' jumbles gent's, the key letter follows, and 'collecting' wraps the identity papers round both.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body by swallowing.

clue.text: Peter has tiny carved 'P' inside napkin holder

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: inside says the letter P goes within the rearranged letters
carved means cut up, so the letters of tiny are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Peter has whittled a tiny letter P to hold a table napkin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved' rearranges tiny and P goes 'inside' it. Napkin is British for a baby's nappy, which this pin fastens.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a British word for a nappy or diaper, traditionally fastened with a large clasp pin.

clue.text: Keen on learning in workshop with American

parts.note: a studio is an artist's workshop
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An eager student takes a workshop with an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person is devoted to study and eager to acquire knowledge.

clue.text: Huge performance taking on worker in charge

indicators.note: taking on means the performance word adds the worker after it

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
a worker ant, a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: A massive concert hires a worker to run it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, a synonym for huge.

clue.text: With nothing I make celebrity status

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA (sweet Fanny Adams), British slang for nothing at all
me is the object form of I, the speaker

explanation.surface: A self-made person claims to have become famous from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame is the condition of being widely known, which is what celebrity status is.

clue.text: Shrink uses humour on woman

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the humour word sits above, before the woman

parts.note: wit is clever humour
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist uses humour on a female patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' looks like a psychiatrist but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither is to shrivel up and dry, so to shrink.

clue.text: Goods in jade sculpted with sharp edges

indicators.note: in says the goods letters go inside the reshaped stone
sculpted means shaped anew, so the letters of jade are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
G is short for good, so GG is goods

explanation.surface: Goods carved from jade end up with sharp edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpted' reshapes the letters of jade and 'in' sets the goods letters within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Jagged means having rough, sharp projections along its edge.

clue.text: Fit windows in government lounge

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about idly

explanation.surface: New windows are installed in a government lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room, but it is the verb meaning to idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To glaze is to fit panes of glass into window frames.

clue.text: Playful comedy sketch about West End is hard to follow

indicators.note: to follow says the hard letter comes after the others

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

indicators.note: End means the last letter of the word West

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch about London's West End is difficult to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district, but here it is just the end of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish means lively and frivolous, as a playful, excitable horse is.

clue.text: Strain when part of reprieve is held up

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says only a run of letters from these words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone under strain gets a partial reprieve, though it is delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Strain when part' took in the indicator; 'Strain' alone is the definition, 'when' a link and 'part of' the hidden-word signal. EVEIS read upward in this down clue gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain liquid is to pass it through a mesh utensil, so the verb sense matches.

clue.text: French president's importing top grade Italian pasta

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the grade goes inside the president's name

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is President of France; the 's means 'is'
A is the top grade in a marking scheme

explanation.surface: France's president imports first-rate Italian pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks part of the definition but supplies the final letter; Emmanuel Macron is France's president.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a type of short tubular noodle, one of the commonest kinds of pasta.

clue.text: Dash to get publicity round hotel by noon

indicators.note: round says the publicity word goes around the hotel letter

parts.note: hype is extravagant publicity
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hurried rush to get press attention around a hotel by midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a hurry but is the punctuation mark; 'round' wraps the publicity word round the hotel letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a short horizontal line in punctuation, like the joining stroke between compound words.

clue.text: Pub landlady cooked nice eels

indicators.note: cooked means prepared, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The woman running the pub has made a dish of tasty eels.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the holder of a licence to sell alcohol runs a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's landlord or landlady holds the licence to sell alcohol on the premises.

clue.text: Stream series available at last in the Netherlands

parts.note: a run is a series, as a run of wins

indicators.note: in says that final letter goes inside the country code

parts.note: NL is the international vehicle code for the Netherlands

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word available

explanation.surface: A television series is finally available in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A runnel is a small brook or rivulet, a little stream.
